In 'Chapter 11: World Percussion', tell me about: 11.3 Layering independent voices

A percussion ensemble is several `beat` patterns playing *at the same time*. Each call to `beat` sets a looping pattern for *one drum sound*. You layer them by calling `beat` multiple times in sequence — the patterns all loop together, locked to the same tempo and measure grid.

Here's a simple two-voice African-style pattern: a low drum (kick) playing a steady pulse, and a high drum (hihat) playing an offset pattern.

[code omitted — see next turn]

Grid labeled with beat numbers 1-2-3-4 underneath. Note-sprite decoration: a few eighth-note glyphs (16×16 shrunk) bopping along the hihat line, quarter-note glyphs (also 16×16) on the kick line — subtle, ambient, synced to the sounding beats.]

`<!-- BUILD: render beat-grid visualization for the two patterns; place note-sprite glyphs (16×16 eighths and quarters) that bop in time with the scheduled hits -->`

**Why it locks:** both patterns share the same transport tempo and measure length. The kick pattern has 8 steps (eighth-note grid, but only hits on even steps → quarters). The hihat pattern has 8 steps, hitting on different offsets. They loop at the same rate, so they stay in phase.

**To add more voices, call `beat` more times:**

Each pattern is a list of steps. The lists can be *different lengths* (the engine will figure out the least-common-multiple measure to keep them in phase), but for clearest results, keep them all the same subdivision (all eighths, or all sixteenths) and vary the *placement of hits*, not the grid size.

In instruments, tell me about: 2.5 The sustain pedal — hold the notes ringing

The pedal is what makes the piano *sing*. When the pedal is down,
notes do not damp when their durations expire — they keep ringing
until you release the pedal. This is the defining piano articulation.

[code omitted — see next turn]

Four short notes played in sequence with the pedal down. Even though
each note is only an eighth beat long, they all keep ringing —
because the pedal has kept every damper up. When you release the
pedal on the last line, all four notes damp at once. This is the
"blooming chord from a scale" pattern: play a melodic figure with
the pedal down and every note becomes a chord tone.

```motoi
;; Teleporter pairs
(define grid (ai/grid 6 6))

(define teleporters
  '(((1 1) (5 5))    ;; pair A
    ((2 3) (4 1))))  ;; pair B

(define (find-partner x y)
  (let loop ((pairs teleporters))
    (cond
      ((null? pairs) #f)
      ((and (= x (car (car (car pairs))))
            (= y (car (cdr (car (car pairs))))))
       (car (cdr (car pairs))))   ;; return partner
      ((and (= x (car (car (cdr (car pairs)))))
            (= y (car (cdr (car (cdr (car pairs)))))))
       (car (car pairs)))         ;; return other end
      (else (loop (cdr pairs))))))
```

Tell me about: 15.1 The simplest choice: `ai/decide`

The humblest director is a function that looks at the world and returns a behavior to run. `ai/decide` takes that function and an entity, calls it every tick, and applies whatever the function returns.

Here's a sprite that wanders unless you get close — then it flees:

```motoi
(let ((sprite (world/spawn 'x 0 'y 0 'sprite 'blossom-plum)))
  (big-bang
    (on-tick
      (lambda (w)
        (world/step)
        (let ((dist (entity/distance sprite
                      (list (world/camera-x) (world/camera-y)))))
          (ai/decide sprite
            (lambda (self)
              (if (< dist 5.0)
                (ai/flee self (list (world/camera-x) (world/camera-y)) 2.0)
                (ai/wander self 0.5 1.0)))))
        'ok))
    (to-draw (lambda (w)
               (grid/dot 0 0 'clear)
               (world/frame)))))
```

<!-- BUILD: wire this as runnable example ch15-ex01-decide-basic.scm; depends on ai/decide + ai/flee + ai/wander from §20 + world/camera-x/y accessor gap -->

*[needs: ai/decide + world/camera-x/y accessor]*

[VISUAL: A plum-blossom sprite wandering in lazy arcs across a pale surface; when the camera (or a touch cursor, in the live app) approaches within 5 cells, the sprite darts away.]

The lambda you pass to `ai/decide` receives the entity and must return a *steering force* — the same `(dx dy)` pair that `ai/seek`, `ai/flee`, and `ai/wander` produce. Every tick, `ai/decide` calls your lambda, takes the force, and applies it to the entity's velocity (respecting `ai/max-force!` if you've set it).

This is the atomic unit of agency: **look at the world, pick a force, apply it.**

```motoi
;; A rat finds the cheese in a small maze.
(define (rat-maze)
  (world/reset!)
  (let ((grid (ai/grid 10 10 32))  ;; 10×10 cells, each 32 pixels
        (rat (world/spawn 'rat 16 16)))
    (entity/sprite! rat 'rat)
    (entity/max-speed! rat 50)
    ;; Build a simple maze: block cells to form walls
    ;; Wall pattern: vertical bar at x=5, with gaps at y=2 and y=7
    (ai/wall! grid 5 0)
    (ai/wall! grid 5 1)
    ;; gap at y=2
    (ai/wall! grid 5 3)
    (ai/wall! grid 5 4)
    (ai/wall! grid 5 5)
    (ai/wall! grid 5 6)
    ;; gap at y=7
    (ai/wall! grid 5 8)
    (ai/wall! grid 5 9)
    ;; Rat starts at (0,0) in grid coords, cheese is at (9,9)
    (let ((path (ai/path grid 0 0 9 9)))
      ;; path is a list of (grid-x grid-y) steps
      ;; Convert to pixel waypoints (center of each cell)
      (let ((waypoints (map (lambda (cell)
                              (let ((gx (car cell))
                                    (gy (cadr cell)))
                                (list (+ (* gx 32) 16) (+ (* gy 32) 16))))
                            path)))
        (ai/waypoints rat waypoints)
        ;; Run until the rat reaches the cheese
        (let loop ((i 0))
          (when (< i 300)
            (world/step 0.016667)
            (loop (+ i 1))))
        (let ((x (entity/x rat))
              (y (entity/y rat)))
          (list 'rat-at x y 'path-length (length path)))))))

(with-seed 1004 (rat-maze))
;; ⇒ (rat-at 304.0 304.0 path-length 19) — found the cheese via the gaps
```
Tell me about: Day-Night Cycle with Behavioral Switching

A global "time" variable cycles between day and night. During the day, sprites forage; at night, they return to a roost and huddle. Predators are active at night, inactive during the day.

```motoi
(begin
  (define time-of-day 'day)
  (define day-timer 0)

  (define roost (world/spawn 12 6))
  (entity/tag! roost 'roost)
  (entity/sprite! roost 'blossom-lotus)
  (entity/pin! roost #t)

  (define (make-forager x y)
    (let ((e (world/spawn x y)))
      (entity/tag! e 'forager)
      (entity/sprite! e 'blossom-bee)
      (entity/max-speed! e 1.5)
      (ai/max-force! e 0.1)
      e))

  (define (make-predator x y)
    (let ((e (world/spawn x y)))
      (entity/tag! e 'predator)
      (entity/sprite! e 'blossom-rose)
      (entity/max-speed! e 2.0)
      (ai/max-force! e 0.15)
      e))

  (make-forager 4 4)
  (make-forager 20 4)
  (make-forager 12 10)
  (make-predator 18 8)

  (define (update-forager f)
    (if (eq? time-of-day 'day)
        (ai/wander f)
        (ai/arrive f (entity/pos roost))))

  (define (update-predator p)
    (if (eq? time-of-day 'night)
        (let ((nearest (world/nearest p 'forager)))
          (if nearest
              (ai/pursue p (entity/pos nearest) (entity/vel nearest))
              (ai/wander p)))
        (ai/wander p)))

  (big-bang
    (on-tick (lambda (s)
               (set! day-timer (+ day-timer 1))
               (when (= (modulo day-timer 200) 0)
                 (set! time-of-day (if (eq? time-of-day 'day) 'night 'day)))
               (group/each 'forager update-forager)
               (group/each 'predator update-predator)
               (world/step)
               s))
    (to-draw (lambda (s) 'grid))
    (with-seed 8014)))
```

The global `time-of-day` toggles every 200 ticks. Foragers check the time: if day, they wander (simulating foraging); if night, they seek the roost. Predators are only active (pursuing foragers) at night; during the day they wander harmlessly. This creates a diurnal rhythm where the scene's behavior shifts with the cycle.

```motoi
;; Associate deals with contacts in batches.
(define (batch-associate pairs batch-size)
  (let loop ((remaining pairs) (results '()))
    (if (null? remaining)
        results
        (let ((batch (take batch-size remaining))
              (rest (drop batch-size remaining)))
          (let ((result (crm/assoc-batch batch)))

                  (cons (if (equal? result 'nan)
                            (list 'batch batch 'status 'failed)
                            (list 'batch batch 'status 'success))
                        results)))))))
```

```motoi
;; Key-door puzzle state
;; grid: 0=empty, 1=wall, 2=red-door, 3=blue-door
;; state: (x y keys) where keys is a list of colors
(define (can-move? grid state dx dy)
  (let ((x (car state))
        (y (cadr state))
        (keys (caddr state)))
    (define w (length (car grid)))
    (define h (length grid))
    (define (cell cx cy)
      (if (and (>= cx 0) (< cx w) (>= cy 0) (< cy h))
          (list-ref (list-ref grid cy) cx)
          1))
    (let ((nx (+ x dx))
          (ny (+ y dy))
          (tile (cell (+ x dx) (+ y dy))))
      (cond
        ((= tile 1) #f)  ;; wall
        ((= tile 2) (member 'red keys))
        ((= tile 3) (member 'blue keys))
        (else #t)))))

(define key-grid
  '((0 0 2 0 0)
    (0 1 1 1 0)
    (0 0 3 0 0)
    (0 0 0 0 0)))

(define state-no-keys '(1 0 ()))
(define state-red-key '(1 0 (red)))

(display "Move right (no keys): ")
(display (can-move? key-grid state-no-keys 1 0))
(newline)
(display "Move right (red key): ")
(display (can-move? key-grid state-red-key 1 0))
(newline)
```
